experiment: P5g shared frozen-forward and dense bounded-head execution
research_question: After P5f showed that a selected-row lazy attachment head is not numerically equivalent, can the frozen five-model P5e JNR-only attachment share one frozen base forward while retaining the original dense full-batch attachment head, with exact outputs and a pre-registered end-to-end latency reduction?
single_changed_axis: execution scheduling only: the candidate obtains classification logits and full 12-parameter base output from one frozen model(iq) call; both reference and candidate evaluate the unchanged attachment head densely over every row using the same batching

reference_execution.base_execution: collect frozen posterior then collect full base parameter output
reference_execution.head_execution: unchanged dense frozen attachment on every sample
reference_execution.attachment: write only frozen positive MFT/VFT/ISRJ JNR cells

candidate_execution.base_execution: one frozen model(iq) forward returns logits and normalized all-12 parameters
candidate_execution.head_execution: the identical frozen attachment is evaluated densely on every sample
candidate_execution.forbidden: No selected-row/lazy head, quantization, compilation, batch alteration or architecture claim.

development_data.roles: evaluation-only; no training, selection, calibration or threshold adjustment

benchmark.device: same CUDA device, fixed batch size 126, inference_mode
benchmark.timing: CUDA synchronize before and after every timed repeat; report median, P10, P90 and candidate/reference ratio

stop_rule: If any exact-equivalence or latency gate fails, retain P5e only as dense bounded-attachment evidence. Do not change batch size, timing loop, thresholds, head, feature, weights, normalizer, compiler, quantization or scheduling on P5g development identities; do not generate/use confirmation identities.

confirmation_if_and_only_if_development_.decision: Only a pass may support the narrow claim that a shared frozen base forward preserves P5e dense-head outputs while lowering measured inference cost; it is not a new trained backbone or classification claim.
